paper: Shah, Beniwal, Singh, Silpasuwanchai 2026 - Sycophancy as a Multilingual Alignment Failure
research_question: Does sycophancy scale with resource tier; are safety topics affected more; does tokenization mediate?
languages: 38 (19 high, 14 low incl. bn hi gu ne ta te; 5 'zero-shot' incl. as or my km lo)
low_resource_or_vulnerable: Yes (low + zero-shot tiers; Assamese, Odia, Bengali included)
genealogy_analysed: Partly: family as categorical OLS regressor; Appendix D clusters languages by behavioural profile (dendrograms; figures only, text does not compare clusters to families)
crosslingual_transfer_tested: No (single-turn; question and completion in same language)
controls_competence|resource|tokenizatio: competence: NO (no correctness conditioning; opinion prompts) | resource: tier (Joshi 2020) | tokenization: fertility, Spearman planned, values only in appendix | translation: MT (NLLB/Tower/Gemmax) + 2 student annotators per language, kappa 0.725
metrics_design: Forced-choice log-prob between sycophantic vs non-sycophantic completion; 6 open models <=24B; 1.13M instances
supported_findings: Higher sycophancy in zero-shot tier for all 6 models (+11 to +36 pp); family+script add R^2 +0.175 to +0.312 over tier
author_limitations: Static preference not real interaction; <=24B only; literal translation misses cultural sycophancy; no proprietary models
implication_for_us: CLOSEST WORK. 'Low-resource => more sycophancy' and 'family/script explain variance' are ALREADY partially addressed. Our contribution must differ in measurement (knowledge-conditioned, generative multi-turn) and in manipulated variables (L_Q != L_P; pairwise concordance).
verification: full-text (main body + appendix text; figures not viewed)

paper: Aldahlawi, Rahman, Ahmad 2026 - Influence of Language on Sycophantic Behavior
research_question: How does prompt language affect sycophancy prevalence and form?
languages: en, ar, zh, fr, es, pt
controls_competence|resource|tokenizatio: competence: N/A (opinion tweets, no ground truth) | resource: no | tokenization: no | translation: GPT-4o MT, not human-validated except 50 en + 50 ar responses
metrics_design: Stance judged by GPT-4o; Language-Exclusive Sycophancy (LES) metric; 3 hosted models
supported_findings: Language effect significant for all models (chi-square); Arabic dominates LES for Claude and GPT
author_limitations: 3 proprietary models only; curated opinions; GPT-4o judge; non-en/ar unchecked by natives
implication_for_us: Shows language-dependent sycophancy exists for high-resource languages; no Indic, no correctness.

paper: Hong et al. 2025 - SYCON Bench
research_question: Multi-turn sycophancy under sustained pressure
metrics_design: Turn of Flip, Number of Flip; 17 LLMs; debate / unethical stereotypes / false presuppositions
supported_findings: Sycophancy prevalent; alignment tuning amplifies; scale/reasoning help; third-person framing reduces (abstract: up to 63.8% in debate)
implication_for_us: Source of multi-turn metrics (ToF/NoF) and a mitigation baseline (third-person framing). Code public.

paper: Sinha 2026 - SycoBench-600
research_question: Resistance to social pressure and correction selectivity
controls_competence|resource|tokenizatio: competence: baseline answer recorded; valid-correction control included
metrics_design: 600 four-option MCQs, doubt / authority / explicit wrong suggestion; 7 assistants
supported_findings: Willingness to update != selectivity (abstract)
implication_for_us: Direct template for our valid-correction control and selectivity metric; English anchor to validate pipeline.

paper: Maraia, Zanzotto, Ranaldi 2026 - Sounding vs Being an Expert
research_question: Separate explicit authority vs register vs culture in sycophancy
controls_competence|resource|tokenizatio: competence: YES - 'Golden Set' of ~500 questions each model answered correctly (single answer, no permutation) | translation: professionally validated EU20-TruthfulQA
metrics_design: 'Sycophancy Matrix' on TruthfulQA subset; open models
supported_findings: Formal register can trigger more deference than credentials; 'fingerprints' tied to model family not language (abstract)
author_limitations: Golden Set restricts to knowledge abandonment; cultural cause not isolated; scope limited to Indo-European languages where deference is lexical
implication_for_us: Knowledge-conditioning in multilingual sycophancy ALREADY DONE (weaker single-answer form) => our KCS is a refinement, not a contribution. Their stated limitation (Indo-European only) supports extending to non-IE Indian comparators.

paper: Ranaldi & Pucci 2026 - Multilingual Agentic Policy to Control Sycophancy
research_question: Train a policy (answer / counter / clarify) to resist sycophancy
languages: 11 languages (incl. en, it, es, zh, sw per Table 3); multilingual variants MMMLU-Redux, MGSM-Symbolic
crosslingual_transfer_tested: YES on two readings: (a) mitigation trained on English instances 'generalise[s] beyond it' (Fig. 3); (b) 'multilingual action consistency' = same action for same query across language pairs (Table 3; base Llama-3-8B En∩It 34%, En∩Sw 15%). Query fully in one language; L_Q = L_P.
controls_competence|resource|tokenizatio: No knowledge gate described for consistency table; no resource/tokenization/genealogy controls
supported_findings: Sycophancy higher in multilingual variants; English-trained policy generalises; base model has low cross-lingual action consistency, lowest for distant/lower-resource pair (Sw)
author_limitations: Fixed interaction horizon; model-based simulated users and judges
implication_for_us: WEAKENS NOVELTY of T3 (intervention transfer: largely addressed) and of T1 (item-level cross-lingual behavioural concordance: partially addressed, 5 languages, one model, no controls). Remaining distinct piece for H3 = genealogy vs controlled confounds.

paper: Huang & Cheng 2026 - Symbolic Power of Languages via Persuasion Simulation
research_question: Quantify language prestige via LLM persuasion outcomes
languages: India: en, hi, bn, te, ta; Morocco; Malaysia; plus single-language countries
metrics_design: GPT-4o persuader/persuadee role-play; Symbolic Power Index; OLS on social factors
supported_findings: Reproduces prestige hierarchy: English > Hindi > Bengali; Tamil/Telugu disadvantaged; misses regional prestige
author_limitations: Single model; simulation of people, not assistant behaviour
implication_for_us: PRIOR EVIDENCE FOR OUR H2 (status). Our study differs: assistant abandoning KNOWN factual answers, with pushback language manipulated independently of question language.

implication_for_us: Shows cultural framing confound; our templates must be minimal and culturally neutral.

paper: Qi, Fernandez, Bisazza 2023 - Cross-Lingual Consistency of Factual Knowledge
research_question: What drives cross-lingual consistency of factual knowledge?
supported_findings: Genetic sim moderate r~0.42-0.52; geographic weak; syntactic none (BMLAMA-17); subword vocabulary overlap r~0.70-0.80 'overshadowing the effect of genetic similarity'
author_limitations: Noisy typological vectors for low-resource languages
implication_for_us: KEY COMPETING EXPLANATION: any genealogy effect we find must survive a subword-overlap control.

paper: Awuni, Gyening, Owusu 2026 - AfriSyCo
research_question: Do models switch answers on African-language factual items under assertive pushback; effect of framing, verification and wording
languages: Hausa, Igbo, Kinyarwanda, Swahili, Twi, Yoruba (+ English follow-ups)
crosslingual_transfer_tested: PARTIAL L_Q != L_P: factorial keeps item in African language with ENGLISH follow-up framing; separate native-language follow-up layer with different (non-equivalent) templates. No same-content English-vs-native contrast; post-hoc reconciliation +2.4 pp, 95% CI [-0.02, 4.92], authors: 'not an equivalence test', layers 'not pragmatically equivalent'
controls_competence|resource|tokenizatio: competence: turn-1 correct (authors: 'not evidence of stable or latent knowledge'); one deterministic option rotation stability subset (611 obs) | translation: IrokoBench human translations; native templates reviewed by 2 streams, kappa 0.59 | neutral re-ask condition in native layer
metrics_design: AfriMMLU-derived MCQ; 7 open 8-12B checkpoints; greedy; 1,415 obs from 100 questions; question-clustered inference
supported_findings: Assertive framing +30.4 pp target selection; verification -17.4 pp; checkpoint effects 9.2-47.0 pp
author_limitations: Results tied to wordings/checkpoints/languages; ethics determination pending; per-language kappa unstable
implication_for_us: CLOSEST WORK TO H2. Pushback in a language other than the question is NOT new. What remains: controlled, same-content manipulation of pushback language (L_Q vs English vs regional dominant) on permutation-gated known items, with placebo and comprehension controls, in Indian languages.

paper: Huang 2026 - Anatomy of LLM Sycophancy: What a Flip Rate Hides (SycoLens)
research_question: What does a single flip rate conceal?
controls_competence|resource|tokenizatio: competence: screening with 21 draws balanced over option order; matched control deleting pushback line (subtracts at-rest churn); memoryless redraw null; decision-boundary distance
metrics_design: ~760k replays, 11 frontier models; moral vignettes + arithmetic
supported_findings: Effects several times larger near decision boundary; screening-consistent items still carry ~half of largest effects; flips on minority-side commitments 'mostly measure regression toward the model's own distribution'
author_limitations: Finite-sample screening label (13% minority probability compatible with 21 agreeing draws)
implication_for_us: WEAKENS H1 NOVELTY: guess/boundary inflation of flip rates and matched no-pushback controls already argued in English. Our H1 becomes a cross-lingual application/robustness check, not a headline.

paper: Noshin et al. 2026 - BenSyc
research_question: Conversational (social) sycophancy benchmark for Bengali contexts
controls_competence|resource|tokenizatio: No correctness; GPT-5.5 judge; 2 native annotators, kappa 0.76
metrics_design: Classification + generation over 1,078 Reddit posts; >15 models
supported_findings: Generation sycophancy up to 92.5% (Llama3.3-70B) on social posts
author_limitations: May not generalise; Reddit bias; judge reliability
implication_for_us: Regional prior work (Bengali) on SOCIAL sycophancy; no overlap with factual capitulation, H2 or H3. Must be cited; Banglish relevant to script-twin idea.

paper: Gupta, Jindal, Nigam, Sood 2026 - Are You Sure You're Sure? Two Confounds
research_question: Audit of SycEval timing effect
controls_competence|resource|tokenizatio: Shows template confounds: naming a target answer raises follow rate 14.1-49.5 pp; format-instruction placement flips effects
supported_findings: Timing effect reverses once target naming is equalised
implication_for_us: DESIGN CONSTRAINT: every pushback condition we compare must name the target identically and keep format instructions in the same place; otherwise L_P effects are confounded.
